chapter.title: Exam Week
chapter.sub: Every day at four, the exam rooms' microphones lose an argument with twelve cameras.
chapter.status: **DRAFT** · scripted from the series plan · IDs provisional

items.text: SEASON 5 · EPISODE 4 · DRAFT · CASE-029  Countdown · Maya, Wes, Officer Delgado and Tomas · Level L4 · Intermediate support  Exam week. Every three minutes after 4:00, the microphones in four proctored rooms reboot and the proctors go silent mid-sentence. Security’s new cameras are misbehaving in the same rooms, at the same minute.  ⚑ RV-127: PoE figures simplified. RV-128: security owns the cameras. Some choices run on a clock.

items.title: Exam Week
items.stakes: Every three minutes, four exam rooms go silent. The switch is Tomas's, the cameras are Delgado's, and 180 students are counting on a voice saying how long is left.
items.clock: Before the exams end at 5:00 — and before tomorrow's 4:00.
items.reward: Proctors who can be heard. Delgado's trust. A switch that isn't asked for more than it has.

objectives.text: Get the owners in one room
Look closer: two things about the cameras

items.rumor: The mics are fine. The cameras are fine. Something in between is being asked for too much.

items.alt: A proctored exam hall at 4:00 p.m.: rows of single desks, a wall clock, two ceiling microphone arrays whose lights have just turned red. The proctor's announcement stops mid-word.
items.caption: Room 203. The ceiling mic dropped the proctor's voice mid-word — and the hearing loop with it.

lines.text: It's the third time since four. Room 203's proctor is writing the time on the board with a marker.
Good proctor. Now let's be as good as she is.

items.alt: The AV operations office. Four room tiles on the wall blink red in a row. Wes on the phone with a proctor; Maya turning from her desk.

bubbles.text: Rooms 201 to 204. Mics went down at four, came back, down again at 4:03.
Every three minutes. Something's keeping time.

items.prompt: Should I just reboot them again? They come back every time.

options.label: “They come back and go down again. Let's keep the proctors talking first, then ask the switch why.”
options.reply: Handhelds. Right. I'll grab the case.

options.label: “What do you think is happening?”
options.reply: Something happens every three minutes. I'd look at whatever keeps time.

items.text: ✦ UX RULE #45 · AVERY'S LENS  Temporary is a promise with a date  Every temporary change needs an owner, an expiry date and a check that it ended.  The cameras went on the AV switch ‘temporarily’ in October. The new switch sat in its box for six weeks.

items.prompt: 4:04. Four exams, 180 students, fifty-six minutes left. What do you do first?
items.risk: Students who can't hear the time.
timeout: The proctors needed a voice that didn't depend on the switch.

hints.text: What would keep the proctors heard whatever the switch does?

options.label: Keep rebooting the microphone arrays
options.result: They come back at 4:05 and drop again at 4:06.
options.fail: The cause hasn't changed; neither will the result.

options.label: Get the proctors battery handheld mics on portable speakers and times on the board — then ask the switch why
options.result: Wes runs the handheld case up the stairs. At 4:11 Room 203 hears “forty-nine minutes remaining.”
options.consequence: The exam no longer depends on the switch while you find out.

options.label: Unplug the new cameras in the closet
options.result: Tomas and Delgado both find out within the hour.
options.consequence: Two owners' equipment, touched without asking.
options.fail: The switch is Tomas's; the cameras are Delgado's.

options.label: Ask the exams office to stop the exams
options.result: Four hundred minutes of students' work, stopped by a microphone.
options.consequence: A bigger harm than the one you have.

items.alt: Tomas's switch shows its PoE log in a read-only view: at 16:00:04 the budget was exceeded and ports 21–24 — the microphones, priority LOW — were shed; they came back at 16:03 and were shed again at 16:06. Draw: 490 W of 370.
items.caption: The switch isn't broken. It's being asked for 120 watts it doesn't have.

items.title: Four o'clock, every day.
items.body: The reboots started at 4:00 yesterday too, and the day before. At 4:00 in December, the new cameras switch to night mode: infrared on, 13 W becomes 25 W, twelve times over. Microphones don't keep a schedule. Cameras do.
items.label: Test: what happens at 4:00 — and what does it rule out?

items.alt: Room 201 during a break: Delgado points up at a dome camera whose ring of infrared emitters has switched on. A label: IR ON, 25 W.

bubbles.text: Night mode at four. It's how they see in the dark.
And how the switch runs out of power. Can they run in day mode while the lights are on?

items.title: Eight small red lights
items.body: Up close, each dome camera has a ring of infrared emitters — invisible to people, bright to a camera. At 4:00 they glow faint red through Wes's phone camera. Delgado: “They switched on at four yesterday too. I thought that was the point.” It is. It's also twelve more watts each.

items.sub: Intermediate · the skill behind this chapter

items.alt: A teaching moment: Maya and Wes beside a board. PoE budget: add up every port's watts. Headroom is the budget minus what's used. Three seventy budget. Twelve new cameras at twenty-five and the old load at one ninety… Four ninety used, minus a hundred and twenty headroom. The switch picks who loses power.

bubbles.text: PoE budget: add up every port's watts. Headroom is the budget minus what's used.
Three seventy budget. Twelve new cameras at twenty-five and the old load at one ninety…
Four ninety used, minus a hundred and twenty headroom. The switch picks who loses power.

items.caption: Intermediate: the formula and what every letter means. The arithmetic is yours.

items.text: 📗 FIELD NOTES · INTERMEDIATE  Terms   PoE budget   Power over Ethernet   Port priority   Formula and variables   ƒ FORMULA · PoE power budget  P used  = Σ P port  · headroom = P budget  − P used    P port   power drawn at each port, W  P budget   the switch's PoE budget, W  headroom  what's left, W (negative means ports get shut off)     ƒ FORMULA · Percentage  % = part ÷ whole × 100   part  the piece you are measuring  whole  everything it is part of

items.label: **Learn it now:** PoE budgets and port priority.

items.text: 📖 From the Fieldbook · tap a plate to open it full size     Trace energy, data and control     Case study: how one SDI cable took the main camera     The studio camera — controls, ports and layout

items.prompt: 4:30. You know the budget and the minute. What do you do about the cameras and the switch?
unknown: Why the cameras are on the AV switch at all
timeout: You keep the numbers to yourself.
Two owners who never hear the same facts make two different decisions.

hints.text: Whose equipment is each piece — and who has to agree?

options.label: Ask Tomas to set the mic ports to critical
options.result: The cameras get shed instead — and go dark mid-exam. Delgado: “That's an exam-integrity problem, not a fix.”
options.consequence: Moves the harm to someone else's equipment.

options.label: Bring Delgado and Tomas the log and the numbers; Delgado decides day mode for exam hours, Tomas plans the move
options.result: Delgado: “Lights are on in there. Day mode until five.” The reboots stop at 4:24… and 4:36, 4:48 stay quiet.
options.consequence: Each owner decides for their own equipment — with the same numbers in front of both.

options.label: Turn the cameras to day mode from the security console
options.result: You don't have the login — and you shouldn't.
options.consequence: Not your cameras, not your console.

options.label: Order a bigger switch
options.result: It arrives in three weeks. Exams end Friday.
options.consequence: Buys past the cause, too late.

items.title: Power down the data cable
items.body: In 2003 the IEEE approved its first Power over Ethernet standard, allowing about 15 watts per port to travel down ordinary network cable. Phones and wireless access points came first; cameras, microphones and lights followed. Each new device made the same old question matter more: how many watts does this switch really have?

items.alt: System View at 4:00 p.m.: the AV-2F switch asked for 490 W of its 370 W budget — microphones, panels, access points and twelve cameras; security's own SEC-2F switch carries only the hallway cameras.
items.caption: Two switches. One overloaded, one barely used.

items.title: ‘Temporary.’
items.body: Change 1014, 14 October: *cameras on AV-2F temporarily until SEC-2F arrives.* SEC-2F arrived on 3 November. It has been in its box behind the closet door ever since. Nobody owned the word ‘until’.
items.label: Test: what was missing — and who moves the cameras?

items.alt: The change record: cameras onto AV-2F, temporarily, until security's switch arrived. It arrived on 3 November. Installed: blank. Ends on: blank.
items.caption: ‘Until’ with no date is ‘forever’.

lines.text: The contractor told me the new switch was ‘a formality’. I believed him. It's my name on the cameras.
And mine on the microphones. Let's put both our names on the date it ends.

items.label: **Fix it:** plan Tomas's change — give the cameras their own switch.

items.alt: Tuesday evening in the network closet: Tomas holds Wes's printed PoE plan; security's new switch is racked and lit.

bubbles.text: Who did the arithmetic on this?

evidence.label: both switches inside budget at night

items.prompt: Wednesday. How do you stop the next ‘temporary’ doing this?
items.risk: The same shedding in another building.
timeout: The change log keeps its one column.
‘Temporary’ stays a word with no date.

hints.text: What two things would have caught this in October?

options.label: Any PoE device added to a switch needs the owner's budget check at worst-case draw — and every temporary change gets an end date that somebody checks
options.result: Tomas adds an ‘ends on’ column; security's contractor now sends worst-case watts with every camera.
options.consequence: Two gaps, two controls, two owners.

options.label: Ban security equipment from AV switches
Set every mic port to critical everywhere
options.result: Next time, something else goes dark instead.
options.consequence: Priority chooses the loser; it doesn't add watts.

options.label: Nothing — it's fixed
options.result: Change 1014 has three siblings in other buildings.
options.fail: Fixing Carrow doesn't fix the habit.

items.label: **First Fail:** where does the power story go wrong?

items.alt: System View on Wednesday at 4:00 with night mode back on: AV-2F at 265 of 370 W, SEC-2F at 345 of 740 W. Both inside budget.
items.caption: Four o'clock came and went. Nothing rebooted.

items.title: SEC-2F · delivered 3 Nov
items.body: Security's switch sat in its shipping box behind the closet door for six weeks, with the delivery note taped on top: *install — see change 1014.* Change 1014 was the ‘temporary’ one. Tomas adds a column to his change log: *ends on.*

items.alt: Room 203 after the last exam: empty desks, the clock at 5:05. Wes and Maya by the door.

bubbles.text: I'd have rebooted them all afternoon. I'd have felt busy.
Everybody does it once. You did the arithmetic instead. That's the job.

items.alt: Late Thursday night in the AV office, empty except for Wes at a laptop. On screen: PRESET ‘HYBRID v7’ · PUSH TO 40 ROOMS · CONFIRM.

bubbles.text: One click. It's just a better preset. I'll write the change record tomorrow.

items.caption: Next: *Wes.*

items.text: FIELD NOTE —  Add up the watts at worst case — infrared on, heaters running — before anything new goes on a switch. When headroom goes negative the switch chooses who loses. Temporary changes need an owner and an end date.
REFLECTION (optional)  · Wes said rebooting would have made him feel busy. When have you chosen the action that felt productive over the one that found the cause?
